title: Delivery service fee values across mirrored clients and checkout authority
scope: Bounded semantic comparison of the current cashier and call-center delivery checkout request construction, configured delivery-service fee read/write paths, server checkout contract, payable calculation, order snapshot and existing delivery intake test source. Supplemental source context for FIN-016; not a new financial finding or a full delivery workflow audit.
decision: Both active WinUI clients pass the selected service FeePiastres into the request and also pass service ID/name, but the checkout handler converts and uses request.DeliveryFeePiastres directly; it contains no DeliveryServices lookup. The service query separately exposes the configured fee and service CRUD persists nullable fee input without an evident sign/range check in the reviewed handlers. Therefore the selected ID/name is not source-bound to the submitted fee at checkout. This corroborates and scopes the existing FIN-016 signed-fee trust-boundary issue; it does not create a duplicate finding. Whether checkout must re-resolve configured fees, or allow a separately authorized override, is an owner policy question. No live request or persistence effect was executed.

behavior.cashier: SubmitPaymentAsync sends SelectedDeliveryService?.FeePiastres ?? 0 for delivery and separately sends SelectedDeliveryService.Id/Name. Non-delivery sends 0.
behavior.callCenter: SubmitOrderAsync sends SelectedDeliveryService.FeePiastres ?? 0 and separately sends its ID/Name. Both clients are behaviorally aligned in this bounded field mapping.
behavior.configuredService: ListActiveDeliveryServicesAsync projects persisted FeePiastres into DeliveryServiceDto. CreateDeliveryServiceHandler and UpdateDeliveryServiceHandler assign request FeePiastres directly; the inspected handler bodies do not show numeric fee sign/range validation.
behavior.serverCheckout: CheckoutOrderHandler converts request.DeliveryFeePiastres to Money and uses it in comp pre-check and BuildPlan. The full handler source contains no DeliveryServices token/lookup, so the submitted service ID/name do not select or validate the authoritative fee in this path.
behavior.calculationAndSnapshot: ComputePayableTotal adds deliveryFee and clamps negative result to zero; Order.Create snapshots plan.DeliveryFee and payable total. No new arithmetic issue beyond FIN-016 is asserted here.
behavior.existingTest: DeliveryOrderIntakeTests constructs a request with DeliveryServiceId=svc-1 and DeliveryFeePiastres=1000, then asserts the same fee is snapshotted. The test does not seed/resolve a service fee for that ID, and does not compare mismatch/negative/stale fee behavior.

counterevidence_and_limits: Both normal clients read service fee values and send the matching selected service fields in the inspected current source; no ordinary UI inconsistency was found.
Delivery service management requires delivery_manage plus manager-approval policy; direct checkout still requires the pos permission. This is not an unauthenticated bypass.
A restaurant may intentionally allow service-fee overrides; no owner policy was found requiring strict fee equality or disallowing a signed fee.
The existing FIN-016 finding already covers negative submitted fee and bypass of the positive discount/comp gates; this comparison is a supplemental explanation, not a new finding.
No deployed configuration, database constraint, binary behavior, HTTP request, or database transaction was tested.
recommendation: Keep this as a FIN-016 evidence extension. The future repair specification should first establish the fee contract: (A) authoritative service pricing—resolve active service by ID at checkout and derive amount server-side, preserving historical order snapshots; or (B) permitted override—validate finite/in-range signed semantics at the server and require the defined approval/permission for deviations. In either case reject unintended negative/non-delivery fees before side effects and preserve legitimate comp, COD and signed ledger behavior. Add tests for selected fee, stale fee after service update, unknown/inactive service, forged fee, negative and bounds/overflow, with assertions that invalid checkout leaves no order/stock/treasury writes.
required_tests: Client request construction parity: both clients send the selected service ID/name/fee consistently; non-delivery sends zero/null service fields.
Server test with configured service fee differing from submitted fee and stale fee after an update; assert the owner-approved contract (derive, reject, or explicitly authorize override).
Negative fee and non-delivery fee inputs are rejected unless a documented contract explicitly allows them; assert no order, inventory, journal or treasury side effects.
Existing positive-fee, zero-fee, COD, approved comp and delivery order snapshot behaviors remain intact.

limitations: This comparison is scoped to fee identity/authority and parity in current WinUI clients, not all delivery state transitions, delivery print flows, or address UI behavior.
FIN-016 isolated arithmetic evidence is separately preserved; this comparison did not reproduce or execute financial operations.
The SEM-044 area/service field comparison remains the canonical evidence for separate address/service-name mapping; this artifact focuses on numeric fee authority.

Source lookup absence is based on reading the full current CheckoutOrderHandler source at the recorded hash and observing no DeliveryServices use; it is not a claim about external middleware or deployed modifications.
